title: A normal subgroup meeting a maximal torus finitely is finite
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $H$ be a reductive affine $F$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $S\subseteq H$ be a split maximal torus, with reductivity and maximal tori as in [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure]. Let $N\subseteq H$ be a closed normal subgroup scheme [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]; normal means that $hnh^{-1}\in N(A)$ for every commutative $F$-algebra $A$, $h\in H(A)$ and $n\in N(A)$. If the scheme-theoretic intersection $N\times_H S$ is finite over $F$, then $N$ is finite over $F$. Here finite means that the coordinate algebra is finite-dimensional over $F$. No smoothness, connectedness or reducedness of $N$ is assumed. The trivial group and a torus $H=S$ are included.

source.place: Corollary 17.85, printed p.379; Corollary 21.53, printed p.441; reduction of the kernel in 23.24, printed p.492. Supporting formulation for arbitrary closed normal subgroup schemes, by applying these results to the reduced identity component over the algebraically closed (hence perfect) field.

proof.text: Put $C=N^\circ$ and $M=C_{\mathrm{red}}$. By [lem-sfb-locally-algebraic-group-identity-component], $C$ is an open and closed subgroup of $N$, and $M$ is a smooth connected finite-type subgroup with $|M|=|C|$. The reduction inclusion is closed by [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction]. Composing the closed inclusions into $H$ using [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-products] and applying [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-affine-cover-criterion] shows that $N,C,M$ are affine. Thus $M$ is a smooth connected closed subgroup of $H$.

source.place: Propositions 1.34 and 1.38, Corollary 1.39, printed pp.16-18; reduced-identity-component reduction in 23.24, p.492.

proof.text: For $h\in H(F)$, normality of $N$ makes conjugation by $h$ an automorphism of $N$, with inverse conjugation by $h^{-1}$. It fixes the identity, hence preserves its connected component $C$. On coordinate rings this automorphism preserves nilpotent elements, so it preserves $M=C_{\mathrm{red}}$ as a subgroup scheme, not merely its $F$-points. Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-ambient-normality-geometric] with ambient group $H$ and algebraic closure $F$ itself: $H$ is smooth by reductivity. It follows that $M$ is normal in $H$.

source.place: Proposition 1.52 and Corollaries 1.85-1.87, printed pp.22 and 32; 23.24, p.492.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-connected-normal-subgroup-reductive] to $M\subseteq H$: all its smoothness, connectedness, closedness and normality hypotheses hold by Steps 1-2. Thus $M$ is reductive. Apply [lem-sfb-normal-subgroup-maximal-torus-intersection] to $G=H$, its normal subgroup $M$, and the given maximal torus $S$. It gives the split maximal torus $R=((M\times_H S)_{\mathrm{red}})^\circ\subseteq M$, with closed inclusion $R\subseteq M\times_H S$.

The inclusion $M\subseteq N$ induces a closed immersion $M\times_H S\to N\times_H S$ by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. Its composite with $R\to M\times_H S$ is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-products]. Write $N\times_H S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ with $A$ finite-dimensional by hypothesis. The affine closed-immersion criterion [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-affine-cover-criterion] expresses $F[R]$ as a quotient of $A$, hence finite-dimensional. If $R\simeq\mathbf G_m^r$ had $r>0$, its Laurent coordinate monomials $1,t_1,t_1^2,\ldots$ would be linearly independent, a contradiction. Thus $r=0$ and $R=1$.

source.place: Corollary 17.85 and the finite-intersection hypothesis; explicit finite-dimensional quotient and split-torus coordinate calculation.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-reductive-torus-self-centralizer] to the reductive group $M$ and its maximal torus $R=1$. It gives $C_M(1)=1$ as subgroup functors on all commutative $F$-algebras. Every element commutes with the identity after every algebra extension, so $C_M(1)(A)=M(A)$ for every $A$. Therefore $M=1$ as a group scheme.

source.place: Proposition 17.61(a), printed p.372, applied to the rank-zero maximal torus.

proof.text: Since $|C|=|M|$, Step 5 makes $C$ a one-point space. By [lem-sfb-group-neutral-component-translates], $N$ has finitely many open and closed connected components, each a translate of $C$. Thus $|N|$ is finite discrete. Its nonempty irreducible closed subsets are singletons, so its topological Krull dimension is zero. The dimension comparison [lem-pc-scheme-dimension-local-rings] gives the same scheme dimension. Apply [lem-pc-algebraic-dim-zero-affine-finite] to the finite-type $F$-scheme $N$ to obtain finiteness. By [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], over $\operatorname{Spec}F$ this says exactly that $F[N]$ is finite-dimensional. Nilpotents in $N$ have not been discarded in this last application.

source.place: Dimension discussion before Proposition 1.37, printed pp.17-18, and Propositions 11.1-11.2, pp.209-210; Stacks Tag 06LH, varieties.tex, lemma-algebraic-scheme-dim-0.

proof_origin.place: Corollaries 17.85 and 21.53 with the reduced-identity-component reduction of 23.24; Proposition 17.61(a) supplies the rank-zero conclusion; Propositions 11.1-11.2 supply final finiteness.
